name: Drostanolone

lead: Drostanolone, widely known as Masteron, is an injectable anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. Medically it was tested in the 1960s to 1980s as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an add-on for a lean, dry, hard look and as a way to limit estrogen-related effects.
The only human trials found are in breast cancer. No published study has measured its effect on physique, face or skin in healthy users, so the claims on forums rest on user reports.

paras: It is a 2-alpha-methyl derivative of DHT, so it activates the androgen receptor and is not converted to estrogen by aromatase. The propionate ester is the usual injectable form.[1][2]

Breast-cancer trials judged side effects generally not serious in that setting.[3] Forum users warn about hair loss in those predisposed, since DHT-derived compounds are not blocked by finasteride or dutasteride in their account, and about skin and cardiovascular effects of stacks.[4][5] It is detected in anti-doping controls and prohibited in sport.[6]

lead: Drostanolone (also dromostanolone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid that is a 2-alpha-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone. It is most often seen as drostanolone propionate, sold historically as Masteril and in bodybuilding circles as Masteron.[1][2][3]

Clinically it was evaluated as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer in randomized trials from 1968 onward, where it was compared with oophorectomy, nandrolone, testolactone, ethinyl estradiol and tamoxifen.[4][5][2][6][7] In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums, it is discussed for a hard, dry look when lean and as an add-on to testosterone or other compounds.[8][9][10]

No study has tested drostanolone for cosmetic outcomes. The human evidence consists of breast-cancer trials and anti-doping research, while community claims about its effect on skin, facial structure, hair and estrogen control come from user reports.
infobox: Controlled / prohibited in sport; not marketed for general use

paras: Drostanolone propionate (Masteril) was tested in breast cancer in a trial from 1968 to 1972 against oophorectomy in premenopausal patients, nandrolone phenylpropionate in perimenopausal patients and ethinyl estradiol in postmenopausal patients; response rates were 44 percent versus 22 percent in the premenopausal group, 34.5 percent versus 39 percent in the perimenopausal group and 38.5 percent versus 57 percent in the postmenopausal group, and the authors described side effects as generally not serious.[2] Other randomized studies compared drostanolone with nandrolone, testolactone and testosterone decanoate, finding similar response rates, with added cyclophosphamide raising response rates in the combination arms.[4][5][6] A 1982 French trial in postmenopausal women found that hormonal therapy with tamoxifen plus drostanolone produced the best immediate objective responses and the fewest adverse effects compared with CMF chemotherapy or the combination.[7] An enanthate ester was used as an anticancer steroid, and a laboratory study examined cytotoxic effects of its microbial metabolites.[11]

On looksmaxxing forums, drostanolone is described as giving a drier, harder look and as a compound some think aids masculinisation when lean. A teenager's post asked whether it was a good compound for looksmaxxing alongside a large stack that included skincare and retinoids; replies were mixed, with one user warning that combining high-strength retinoids and isotretinoin could damage skin.[8] Another thread asked if a five-month course was worthwhile, with replies saying it can look good when lean but may harm hair follicles depending on genetics.[9] A third described using it in place of an aromatase inhibitor to manage estrogen-related effects.[10] A fourth thread compared it with oxandrolone.[12] None of these claims has been tested in a trial.

Clinical studies are limited to randomized breast-cancer trials from 1968 to 1982 comparing drostanolone propionate with oophorectomy, nandrolone, ethinyl estradiol, testololactone and testosterone decanoate, or combining it with tamoxifen or cyclophosphamide.[2][6][5][4][7] No human study has examined it for appearance.

In breast cancer, randomized trials from the 1970s reported objective response rates of roughly a quarter to a half of patients depending on the comparison and whether chemotherapy was added, with no clear difference among the androgens compared.[5][2][4] No randomized trial has evaluated drostanolone for muscle, leanness, skin or facial appearance.

The breast-cancer trials reported that side effects were generally not serious and rarely contraindicated its use in that setting.[2] Information on adverse effects in healthy users is otherwise limited to forum reports. Users cite possible scalp hair loss in genetically predisposed people, and one stated that finasteride and dutasteride do not counteract DHT-derived compounds.[9] Another user reported bloating and mood changes on a testosterone-based regimen without an aromatase inhibitor.[10]

A study of hamsters found that animals self-administered drostanolone, along with nandrolone, oxymetholone and stanozolol, into the brain ventricles, which researchers have used in work on the reinforcing properties of anabolic steroids.[13] Drostanolone has been identified among frequently detected anabolic steroids in doping control.[14]

Drostanolone is 2-alpha-methyl-DHT. Two crystal polymorphs of the propionate ester have been characterised by X-ray diffraction.[1] Because it is 5-alpha-reduced it is not a substrate for aromatase, and Grokipedia describes it as having anti-estrogenic effects used historically in breast cancer; its actual effect on systemic estrogen levels in users has not been shown in published trials.[3] Urinary metabolites have been characterised in humans for doping control, and a methylated derivative, methyldrostanolone, has been identified in commercial products.[14][15][16][17] Seized steroid products have been analysed by NMR for adulteration.[18]

Bodybuilding surveys in Flanders from 1988 to 1993 found 38 to 58 percent of controlled athletes positive in some federations, with the pattern of drugs shifting over time.[19] On looksmaxxing forums, drostanolone appears in teenagers' and young adults' stacks and in debates over whether DHT-derived androgens help or harm facial appearance and hair.[8][9]

lore.intro: Drostanolone is discussed on looksmax.org as a hardening, drying compound and as an estrogen-control add-on, with recurring concern about hair loss.[8][9][10]

claims.claim: Masteron gives a dry, hard, lean look.
Masteron can replace an aromatase inhibitor for controlling estrogen.
It may cause hair loss that finasteride cannot block.
Collagen and skin products can offset the skin effects of a large steroid stack.

timeline.event: A South African trial of drostanolone propionate (Masteril) in breast cancer begins, running to 1972.[2]
Randomized comparisons with testosterone decanoate and testololactone in disseminated breast cancer are published.[4]
Drostanolone propionate is compared with nandrolone decanoate in breast carcinoma.[6]
A French randomized trial tests tamoxifen plus drostanolone against chemotherapy.[7]
